question: How would you approach a low-level design round like 'design a parking lot', using this project as the example?
answer_hinglish:
LLD round mein code se pehle ek order follow karta hoon: requirements -> nouns (entities) -> har entity ki responsibility -> jo cheezein lot-to-lot badalti hain unhe policy (Strategy) banana -> errors -> phir "extend karo" waale follow-ups ke liye ready rehna.

Is project mein yahi kiya. Requirements: teen vehicle types (motorcycle, car, truck), teen spot sizes (small, compact, large), levels, ticket on entry, fee on exit, availability board. Nouns se classes nikli: ParkingLot (rules enforce karta hai aur state ka owner hai), ParkingSpot (ek spot aur uski state), Ticket aur Receipt (frozen data), aur do policies -- AllocationStrategy (kaunsa spot) aur PricingStrategy (kitna paisa). Time ke liye ek Clock interface.

Phir main interviewer ko batata hoon ki kya fixed rule hai aur kya policy. PLAN.md ka decision: lot sirf woh rules enforce karta hai jo kabhi nahi badalte -- spot free ho, vehicle fit ho, ek plate ka ek ticket. "Kaunsa spot" aur "kitna paisa" lot owner badal sakta hai, isliye woh Strategy hain.

Aakhri step: interviewer ke follow-ups socho. PLAN.md khud kehta hai ki Parking Lot mein asli interview follow-ups mein hota hai -- allocation rule badlo, pricing badlo, do gates ek saath, lost ticket, payment fail. Goal yeh tha ki har follow-up ek chhota, local change ho. Aur jo cheez scope mein nahi hai (database, HTTP API, UI, real payment) use clearly "not built" bolo -- LLD round classes aur responsibilities ke baare mein hai, storage ke baare mein nahi.
why_needed: Bina structure ke LLD round mein log seedha 15 classes bana dete hain (Vehicle, Car, Truck, Level, Floor, Gate, Manager...) aur phir pehle follow-up par design toot jaata hai. Ek order hone se aap har class ko justify kar paate ho.
real_world_analogy: Ghar banane se pehle architect pehle poochta hai kitne log rahenge, kya cheez kabhi nahi badlegi (neev, deewar) aur kya baad mein badal sakte ho (furniture, paint). Allocation aur pricing yahan furniture hain -- badalne layak; "ek spot par ek gaadi" neev hai.
how_it_works: Step 1: requirements aur scope (kya NAHI banana). Step 2: entities aur unka data. Step 3: behaviour kis class mein jaayega (jis class ke paas data hai). Step 4: variation points ko interfaces banao (Strategy). Step 5: failure ko kaise report karoge (error codes). Step 6: tests jo rules prove karein.
in_this_project: PLAN.md ka "Why this project" aur "Decisions" section yahi order dikhata hai. src/parking-lot.ts mein ParkingLot, src/spot.ts mein ParkingSpot, src/allocation.ts aur src/pricing.ts mein do Strategy interfaces, src/clock.ts mein Clock, src/errors.ts mein ParkingError. Stage 1 (domain model, strategies, park / quote / exit) ke 75 tests the; README ke hisaab se ab poore project mein 171 tests pass hote hain. PLAN.md "Not in scope": database, HTTP API, UI, real payment, reservations in advance, EV charging spots.
advantages: Har class ka kaam ek line mein bata sakte ho
Follow-up changes local rehte hain (naya strategy, naya rate)
Scope clear hone se interviewer ko pata hai kya jaan-boojh kar chhoda
disadvantages: Pehle 5 minute requirements par lagte hain, code der se shuru hota hai
Chhota design 'too simple' lag sakta hai agar decisions explain na karo
common_mistakes: Har noun ko class bana dena (Level, Floor, Vehicle subclasses)
Policy (kaunsa spot) ko lot ke andar if-else mein hardcode karna
Database aur API se shuru karna jab round classes ka hai
follow_up_questions: Which requirement would you cut first if you had only 30 minutes?
How would you decide what is a policy and what is a fixed rule?
What would you ask the interviewer before writing any class?

question: What are the main classes in this parking lot design and what is each one responsible for?
answer_hinglish:
Core mein kuch hi pieces hain, aur har ek ka ek kaam hai:

- ParkingLot (src/parking-lot.ts): state ka owner aur rules ka enforcer. Spots ki list, active tickets (entries map), plate -> ticket id map, availability rows. Saare public methods synchronous hain aur pehle sab check karte hain, phir state badalte hain.
- ParkingSpot (src/spot.ts): ek spot -- id (jaise L0-1), level, position, size, aur state free / reserved / occupied, saath mein holder ticket id. Transitions guarded methods se: reserve, confirm, transfer, release.
- Ticket: frozen plain object -- id, normalised plate, vehicle, spotId, level, entryAt (lost ticket ke replacement par replaces bhi).
- Receipt: exit ke baad frozen object -- ticket, exitAt, durationMs, feeMinor, paidMinor, payments.
- AllocationStrategy (src/allocation.ts): choose(vehicle, free) -- kaunsa spot. Do implementations: smallestFitFirst (default) aur nearestFirst.
- PricingStrategy (src/pricing.ts): fee(vehicle, entryAt, exitAt) integer minor units mein. Implementation: HourlyPricing.
- Clock (src/clock.ts): now(). systemClock production ke liye, ManualClock tests ke liye.
- ParkingError (src/errors.ts): ek error class, machine-readable code ke saath.
- types.ts: VehicleType aur SpotSize string unions, aur fits().

Baaki pieces (FreeSpotIndex, EntryGate / ExitGate, PayStation, EventQueue, DisplayBoard) stage 2-3 mein aaye -- woh concurrency, payment aur display ke liye hain, core LLD model ke upar.

Key point interview mein: Ticket aur Receipt mein koi behaviour nahi, woh data hain; behaviour ParkingLot aur ParkingSpot mein hai, kyunki state unke paas hai.
why_needed: Interviewer pehle class diagram aur responsibilities poochta hai. Agar aap har class ka kaam ek line mein nahi bata paate, toh design mein responsibilities mixed hain.
real_world_analogy: Ek mall ki parking: manager (ParkingLot) rules lagata hai, har bay (ParkingSpot) ka apna board hota hai "khaali / booked / bhara", ticket (Ticket) sirf ek parchi hai, aur rate card (PricingStrategy) diwaar par lagta hai jo management badal sakta hai.
how_it_works: ParkingLot constructor layout (levels ki array of sizes) se ParkingSpot objects banata hai, FreeSpotIndex banata hai, aur pricing / allocation / clock inject hote hain. park() = reserve() + confirm(). exit() = beginExit + (cash recordPayment agar kuch due) + commitExit, aur Receipt deta hai.
in_this_project: README ka "Classes" diagram yahi relationships dikhata hai: ParkingLot owns 1..n ParkingSpot, owns 1 FreeSpotIndex, uses 1 AllocationStrategy, 1 PricingStrategy, 1 Clock. src/index.ts sab public exports ek jagah deta hai. Spot ids constructor mein `L${levelNo}-${position + 1}` se bante hain (test: "names spots L<level>-<position from 1>").
advantages: Kam classes, har ek ka clear kaam
Data (Ticket, Receipt) aur behaviour (lot, spot) alag
Policies interface ke peeche, plug-in ho sakti hain
disadvantages: ParkingLot kaafi bada hai (entry, money, exit, lost ticket sab ek class mein)
Vehicle ki apni class nahi, toh vehicle-specific behaviour aaye toh jagah banani padegi
common_mistakes: Vehicle -> Car / Truck inheritance bana dena jab type sirf ek string hai
Ticket ko mutable object rakhna jise caller badal sake
Pricing logic ParkingSpot ya Ticket ke andar daal dena
follow_up_questions: Why is there no Vehicle class?
Would you split ParkingLot? Into what?
Where does the fee calculation live, and why there?

question: How does the design decide whether a vehicle fits a spot?
answer_hinglish:
Ek 3x3 "fits" table rakhne ke bajaye do cheezein hain: spot sizes ek ORDERED array hain (small < compact < large), aur har vehicle ka ek "smallest fit" size hai. Vehicle us size ya usse bade kisi bhi spot mein fit hota hai. Toh fits() bas ek comparison hai: sizeRank(size) >= sizeRank(SMALLEST_FIT[vehicle]).

src/types.ts mein SPOT_SIZES = ["small", "compact", "large"] as const, aur comment kehta hai "The order IS the rule". SMALLEST_FIT = { motorcycle: "small", car: "compact", truck: "large" }. sizeRank bas array index hai. Isse poora table nikalta hai: motorcycle teeno mein, car compact aur large mein, truck sirf large mein.

Kyun aisa? PLAN.md: "Fits is one comparison, not a 3x3 table to keep in sync. Adding a size in between is one array entry." Table hota toh naya size ya vehicle aane par 3 ya 4 jagah cells bharni padti aur ek cell bhoolna aasaan hai. Yahan ek array entry aur ek SMALLEST_FIT entry, baaki apne aap.

Test side par ulta kiya gaya: test/types.test.ts mein poora 3x3 table HAATH se likha hai (9 tests). Comment: "written out by hand so a change to SMALLEST_FIT or to the size order shows up here." Implementation compact hai, test explicit -- dono ek doosre ko check karte hain. README ke mutation checks mein "fits boundary" break (>= ko > karna) stage 1 mein 23 tests, aur stage 3 re-run mein 83 tests fail karta hai.
why_needed: Fit rule har jagah use hota hai: allocation strategies fittingSizes() se sizes chunti hain, aur lot har strategy ka result fits() se dobara check karta hai. Agar yeh rule galat ya inconsistent ho toh truck compact spot mein chala jaayega.
real_world_analogy: Shoe sizes jaisa: agar aapka size 8 hai toh 8, 9, 10 sab pehen sakte ho (dheele sahi), 7 nahi. Har size ke liye alag list rakhne ki zaroorat nahi, bas "mera minimum size" kaafi hai.
how_it_works: SPOT_SIZES.indexOf(size) rank deta hai: small 0, compact 1, large 2. fits(vehicle, size) = rank(size) >= rank(SMALLEST_FIT[vehicle]). fittingSizes(vehicle) = SPOT_SIZES.filter(fits), toh result hamesha smallest first aata hai -- smallestFitFirst strategy isi order par depend karti hai.
in_this_project: src/types.ts: SPOT_SIZES, SMALLEST_FIT, sizeRank, fits. src/allocation.ts: fittingSizes. test/types.test.ts: hand-written expected table. test/allocation.test.ts "lists the sizes each vehicle fits, smallest first": car -> ["compact", "large"], truck -> ["large"]. Lot reserve() mein bhi `!fits(vehicle, spot.size)` check hai, strategy ka result validate karne ke liye.
advantages: Ek rule, ek comparison -- table sync karne ka jhanjhat nahi
Naya size beech mein = ek array entry
Record<VehicleType, SpotSize> se compiler har vehicle ka entry maangta hai
disadvantages: Sirf linear order express hota hai; 'EV spot sirf EV ke liye' jaisa rule isme nahi aata
Array ka order galti se badla toh rule chupchaap badal jaata hai (isliye hand-written test)
common_mistakes: Test mein bhi same formula use karna -- tab test implementation ki copy ban jaata hai
>= ki jagah > likhna (boundary bug, mutation 'fits boundary')
Fit check sirf strategy mein karna aur lot mein dobara na karna
follow_up_questions: What breaks if someone reorders SPOT_SIZES?
How would you model a spot that only EVs may use?
Why is the test table written out by hand instead of generated?

question: Why is money stored as integers in minor units in this design?
answer_hinglish:
Saara paisa integer hai, minor units mein -- paise ya cents. 5000 matlab 50.00. Kahin bhi floating point se paisa calculate nahi hota.

Reason: JavaScript ka number IEEE 754 double hai, aur 0.1 jaisi decimal values binary mein exact store nahi hoti. src/pricing.ts ka comment exactly yahi kehta hai: "no floating point, so 3 x 0.10 never becomes 0.30000000000000004". Ek parking fee mein yeh chhota lagta hai, par jab aap payments ka sum karte ho, fee minus paid nikalte ho, aur receipt par paidMinor == feeMinor compare karte ho, toh ek 0.0000001 ka farak bhi "due hai" bana sakta hai aur barrier nahi khulega.

Is project mein yeh rule teen jagah enforce hota hai. Ek: HourlyPricing constructor har rate ko Number.isSafeInteger aur >= 0 se check karta hai, warna INVALID_RATE (fractional 49.5, negative, NaN, missing -- sab tested). Do: ParkingLot.checkedFee har strategy ke result ko check karta hai -- 12.5, -1, NaN lautaya toh STRATEGY_BUG aur car parked rehti hai (test "rejects a pricing strategy that returns %s, keeping the car parked"). Teen: field names khud unit batate hain -- feeMinor, paidMinor, dueMinor, amountMinor, lostTicketPenaltyMinor.

Display ke waqt hi divide hota hai: demo.ts mein money = (minor / 100).toFixed(2). Matlab calculation integers mein, formatting sirf output par.
why_needed: Billing mein rounding errors user-visible bugs bante hain: galat receipt, "still due 0.0000001", reconciliation mismatch. Integers se addition aur subtraction exact rehte hain.
real_world_analogy: Dukaandaar hisaab "50 rupaye 50 paise" ki jagah "5050 paise" mein likhe toh kabhi aadha paisa ghoomta nahi. Display ke waqt hi wapas rupaye mein likhta hai.
how_it_works: Rates per hour integer minor units mein. fee = started hours x rate, dono integer, toh product integer. Lot bill() mein feeMinor - paidMinor, Math.max(0, ...) -- sab integers. Number.isSafeInteger 2^53 - 1 tak exact guarantee deta hai.
in_this_project: src/pricing.ts: PricingStrategy comment aur HourlyPricing constructor validation. src/parking-lot.ts: checkedFee, Bill { feeMinor, paidMinor, dueMinor }. test/pricing.test.ts "HourlyPricing validation" (negative, fractional, NaN, missing rate) aur "accepts a zero rate (free parking for a type)". PLAN.md decision: "Money is an integer in minor units (paise, cents). No floating point anywhere money is computed." Currency ka koi field nahi hai -- ek lot ek currency maan kar chalta hai.
advantages: Addition / subtraction exact
Equality compare (paid == fee) bharosemand
Field names (xxxMinor) se unit galti kam
disadvantages: Percent discount jaisi cheez mein rounding rule khud decide karna padta hai
Currency ke minor unit alag ho sakte hain (kuch currencies mein 0 ya 3 decimals) -- yahan modelled nahi
common_mistakes: Rupees float mein store karke baad mein round karna
Display wali string ko wapas parse karke calculate karna
Plugged-in strategy ke result par bharosa kar lena bina integer check ke
follow_up_questions: How would you apply a 15% discount without floats?
What happens beyond Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER?
How would you store this in a database column?

question: Why is ParkingSpot a class with methods while Ticket and Receipt are frozen plain objects?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki ParkingSpot ki state badalti hai aur uske transitions ke rules hain, jabki Ticket aur Receipt sirf ek moment ka record hain jo kabhi badalna nahi chahiye.

ParkingSpot ek entity hai: uska id fixed hai par state free -> reserved -> occupied -> free chalti hai, aur holder (kis ticket ke paas hai) badalta hai. Isliye uske fields private hain (current, holder) aur sirf guarded methods se badalte hain -- reserve, confirm, transfer, release. Har method check karta hai ki yeh transition abhi allowed hai aur sahi ticket ne maanga hai, warna SPOT_STATE.

Ticket ek value hai: id, plate, vehicle, spotId, level, entryAt. Issue hone ke baad inme se kuch nahi badalta. Agar badalna ho (lost ticket), toh code naya ticket banata hai ({ ...old, id: randomUUID(), replaces: old.id }), purana edit nahi karta. Isliye Object.freeze. Receipt bhi wahi: exit ka final record, aur uski payments array bhi Object.freeze([...entry.payments]) se copy karke freeze hoti hai.

Ek aur detail: ParkingLot ke andar Entry naam ka private, mutable object hai (status, lock, payments, penaltyMinor) -- woh lot ki internal bookkeeping hai. Bahar sirf frozen Ticket jaata hai. Matlab mutable state lot ke andar band hai, aur caller ke haath jo aata hai use woh badal nahi sakta. Test "tickets are frozen: a caller cannot move its car to another spot" yahi prove karta hai -- spotId assign karne par TypeError.
why_needed: Agar Ticket mutable hota toh caller ticket.spotId badal kar lot ki bookkeeping se alag kahani bana sakta tha. Entity vs value ka farak samajhna LLD ka basic hai.
real_world_analogy: Parking bay ek physical jagah hai jiska board "khaali / bhara" badalta rehta hai (entity). Ticket ek chhapi hui parchi hai -- usme likha badal nahi sakte; kho jaaye toh nayi parchi milti hai (value).
how_it_works: Entity: identity + changing state + guarded behaviour. Value object: sirf data, immutable, change = naya object. Lot internally Entry rakhta hai jo Ticket ko point karta hai, aur status / lock jaisi mutable cheezein Entry mein hain, Ticket mein nahi.
in_this_project: src/spot.ts: ParkingSpot with private current / holder. src/parking-lot.ts: reserve() mein Object.freeze({...}) se Ticket, commitExit() mein Object.freeze se Receipt, reportLost() mein naya frozen ticket with replaces. README: "Ticket, PaymentQuote, ExitQuote, Payment, Receipt and events are frozen plain objects." README stage 1 mutation "ticket not frozen" 1 test se pakda gaya.
advantages: Caller lot ki state ko ticket ke through nahi badal sakta
Mutable state ek jagah (lot + spot) mein band
Value objects ko freely share kar sakte ho
disadvantages: Ticket mein koi helper behaviour nahi (jaise ticket.durationAt(now))
Har change par naya object banana padta hai
common_mistakes: Ticket class mein status field daal dena aur bahar return karna
Receipt freeze karna par andar ki payments array nahi
Spot ka state public field bana dena
follow_up_questions: Is Object.freeze deep? Does it matter here?
Where does the ticket status live if not in Ticket?
Why does reportLost create a new ticket instead of editing the old one?

question: What is plate normalisation here and why is it needed?
answer_hinglish:
normalizePlate() har plate ko ek canonical form mein laata hai: upper-case, spaces aur '-' hata do, phir check karo ki result 1-12 letters ya digits hai. "mh 12-ab 1234" aur "MH12AB1234" dono "MH12AB1234" ban jaate hain.

Kyun zaroori: lot ka ek rule hai "ek plate ka ek ticket" -- ticketIdByPlate map se ALREADY_PARKED check hota hai. Agar normalisation na ho toh wahi car ek baar "MH12AB1234" aur doosri baar "mh-12-ab-1234" likh kar do tickets le sakti hai, do spots block kar sakti hai. src/parking-lot.ts ka comment: "Without this, one car could hold two tickets."

Validation bhi isi mein hai: PLATE_RE = /^[A-Z0-9]{1,12}$/. Empty string, sirf spaces, "MH12*AB", ya 13 characters -- sab INVALID_PLATE (test "rejects %j"). Non-string input bhi "" ban kar reject hota hai.

Yeh ek boundary par hota hai: reserve(), reportLost(), findByPlate() sab raw plate lete hain aur pehli line mein normalizePlate call karte hain. Andar sab jagah sirf normalised plate hai, aur Ticket.plate mein bhi normalised hi store hota hai. Isliye findByPlate("mh 12 ab 1234") wahi ticket deta hai (tested).

README ke mutation checks mein "plate not normalised" stage 1 mein 4 tests aur stage 3 re-run mein 7 tests fail karta hai -- matlab yeh rule properly locked hai.
why_needed: Identity ka koi bhi key (email, plate, phone) agar alag spellings mein aa sakta hai, toh uniqueness check bekaar hai jab tak canonical form na ho.
real_world_analogy: Email "Rahul@Gmail.com" aur "rahul@gmail.com" ek hi inbox hai; signup check karte waqt lower-case na karo toh ek banda do accounts bana leta hai.
how_it_works: raw -> toUpperCase() -> replace(/[\s-]/g, "") -> PLATE_RE test -> canonical string ya INVALID_PLATE. Har public method jo plate leta hai, entry par yahi function chalata hai; andar ke maps (ticketIdByPlate) sirf canonical keys rakhte hain.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: PLATE_RE, normalizePlate (exported, src/index.ts se bhi). Tests: "upper-cases and drops spaces and hyphens", "refuses the same plate twice, in any spelling, and that changes nothing", "findByPlate accepts any spelling of the plate". Ownership verification (documents, plate photo) is project mein modelled nahi hai.
advantages: Duplicate-plate rule har spelling par kaam karta hai
Validation aur canonical form ek function mein
Andar ka code sirf ek format dekhta hai
disadvantages: Rule simple hai: dot, slash ya local scripts wali plates reject ho jaayengi
Galat OCR (O vs 0) ko yeh nahi pakadta
common_mistakes: Sirf lookup par normalise karna, store karte waqt nahi (ya ulta)
Normalised form ke bajaye raw plate ticket par print karna aur phir compare karna
Validation regex ko normalise se pehle chalana
follow_up_questions: Where else in a real system would you normalise identifiers?
How would you handle O vs 0 confusion from a camera?
Should the printed ticket show the raw or normalised plate?

question: Why does every failure throw a ParkingError with a code instead of a plain Error with a message?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki caller ko failure par DECISION lena hota hai, aur decision message parse karke nahi lena chahiye. ParkingError ke paas ek readonly code hai -- ParkingErrorCode union mein se, jaise LOT_FULL, ALREADY_PARKED, INVALID_PLATE, TICKET_NOT_ACTIVE, INVALID_TIME, STRATEGY_BUG, SPOT_STATE.

src/errors.ts ka comment: "One error class with a machine-readable code, so callers (a gate UI, an HTTP layer later) switch on `code` instead of parsing messages." Message insaan ke liye hai aur kabhi bhi reword ho sakta hai; code ek contract hai. Gate ki screen LOT_FULL par "Full for cars" dikha sakti hai, INVALID_PLATE par "plate dobara daalo".

Code ek TypeScript union hai, toh typo compile time par pakda jaata hai -- new ParkingError("LOT_FUL", ...) compile nahi hoga. ParkingError Error ko extend karta hai aur ErrorOptions leta hai, isliye cause chain ho sakta hai (gate DEVICE_FAILED ke saath original device error cause mein deta hai).

Ek important pairing: har ParkingError ka matlab hai "kuch nahi badla" (check everything, then change). Toh code se caller ko do cheezein pata chalti hain: kya galat hua, aur state safe hai -- retry ya user ko message, rollback ki zaroorat nahi.

Tests bhi message nahi, code compare karte hain -- parking-lot.test.ts mein helper code(fn) sirf e.code nikalta hai. Isse message text badalne par tests nahi toot-te. HTTP layer is project mein implement nahi hai; codes ko status mein map karna (LOT_FULL -> 409 jaisa) wahan ka kaam hoga.
why_needed: Errors bhi API ka hissa hain. Agar callers message strings match karein, toh message ka ek shabd badalna production bug ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Hospital mein triage ke color codes -- red, yellow, green. Doctor lambi report padh kar decide nahi karta, code dekh kar karta hai; report baad mein detail ke liye hai.
how_it_works: class ParkingError extends Error { constructor(readonly code: ParkingErrorCode, message, options?) }, name = "ParkingError". Caller: catch (e) { if (e instanceof ParkingError && e.code === "LOT_FULL") ... }. demo.ts ka why() helper yahi karta hai.
in_this_project: src/errors.ts: ParkingErrorCode (har code ke saath comment), ParkingError. README "Errors" table mein har code kab aata hai. test/parking-lot.test.ts ka code() helper. demo.ts: why = (e) => e instanceof ParkingError ? e.code : String(e). Gates DEVICE_FAILED ke saath { cause } pass karte hain.
advantages: Caller code par switch karta hai, message free text reh sakta hai
Union type se typo compile time par pakda jaata hai
Tests stable: message change se nahi toot-te
disadvantages: Ek hi class mein bahut saare codes; naya code jodne par docs aur callers dono update karne padte hain
Code se HTTP status ka mapping abhi kahin nahi hai (HTTP layer built nahi)
common_mistakes: Har error ke liye alag subclass bana dena jab sirf code alag ho
Tests mein message string compare karna
Internal bug (SPOT_STATE) aur user error (INVALID_PLATE) ko same tarah handle karna
follow_up_questions: Which of these codes would be 4xx and which 5xx in an HTTP API?
When would you prefer error subclasses over a code field?
Why is SPOT_STATE described as 'a bug if it ever reaches a caller'?

question: How is the Strategy pattern used for spot allocation, and how does the lot protect itself from a bad strategy?
answer_hinglish:
"Kaunsa spot milega" ek policy hai jo lot owner badal sakta hai, isliye woh ParkingLot ke andar if-else nahi, ek interface hai: AllocationStrategy { name; choose(vehicle, free) }. ParkingLot constructor mein options.allocation leta hai, default smallestFitFirst. Doosri implementation nearestFirst hai. PLAN.md: do strategies isliye ki interface "hypothetical" na rahe -- dono same lot par alag answer dete hain (tested).

Stage 2 ke baad strategy ko poori spot list nahi milti, ek FreeSpots milta hai jiska ek hi method hai: nearest(size). Toh strategy sirf yeh decide karti hai ki KAUNSA SIZE pehle try karna hai; nearest free spot dhoondhna index ka kaam hai.

Lot strategy par blind bharosa nahi karta. reserve() mein:
1. Pehle lot khud LOT_FULL check karta hai -- koi fitting size free hai ya nahi. Agar nahi, strategy ko call hi nahi kiya jaata (test "reports LOT_FULL, not a strategy bug, when nothing fits (the strategy is not even asked)").
2. Phir choose() call hota hai, aur result check hota hai: undefined nahi, isi lot ka spot (spotsById.get(spot.id) === spot), free hai, aur fits(). Kuch bhi galat toh STRATEGY_BUG, aur lot unchanged.

Tests mein ek "bad" strategy undefined, ek string, ek non-fitting spot, aur doosre lot ka spot lautati hai; ek "sticky" strategy pehle dekha hua spot dobara lautati hai jab woh occupied ho chuka. Sab STRATEGY_BUG aur before / after state same. Matlab invariants (free, fits, ek ticket per plate) lot ke paas hain; strategy sirf preference deti hai.
why_needed: Allocation rules lots ke beech badalte hain (mall vs hospital vs truck depot). Strategy se naya rule = nayi file, ParkingLot untouched. Aur validation se ek buggy plug-in lot ko corrupt nahi kar sakta.
real_world_analogy: Valet company (strategy) batati hai gaadi kahan lagani hai, par parking manager (lot) phir bhi check karta hai ki bay khaali hai aur gaadi usme aati hai, tab hi chaabi leta hai.
how_it_works: reserve: normalise plate -> vehicle valid -> plate not taken -> some fitting size has index.nearest(size) -> spot = allocation.choose(vehicle, index) -> validate spot -> phir hi ticket banta hai aur state change. Strategy ka result sirf ek suggestion hai jo lot verify karta hai.

README mutations: S21 "no LOT_FULL pre-check" stage 2 aur stage 3 dono mein 20 tests; S22 "spot of another lot accepted" 1 test; stage 1 "strategy result unchecked" 2 tests.

question: How does HourlyPricing calculate a fee, including the grace period and started hours?
answer_hinglish:
HourlyPricing ek PricingStrategy hai: fee(vehicle, entryAt, exitAt) -> integer minor units. Rules README mein likhe hain aur code exactly wahi karta hai:

1. Har vehicle type ka apna rate per hour (sab required, integer, negative nahi). Tests mein motorcycle 2000, car 5000, truck 10000.
2. Stay grace period tak (including) free hai. graceMinutes: 10 -> 10 minute tak 0.
3. Grace se upar, POORE stay ke har STARTED hour ka charge -- grace minus nahi hota. Isliye 70 min with 10 min grace = 2 hours, 1 nahi. Test comment: "70 minutes is 2 started hours; it is NOT 60 billable minutes (= 1 hour) after subtracting the grace."
4. "Started hour" = Math.ceil(stayMs / HOUR_MS). 1 ms bhi = 1 hour; exactly 60 min = 1 hour; 60 min + 1 ms = 2 hours.
5. Optional dailyCapHours (1-24): har started 24h (entry se gina) mein max utne hours. Cap 8 par 25h = 8 + 1 = 9 hours.
6. Exit entry se pehle (ya NaN) -> INVALID_TIME.

Grace "whole stay" kyun? Policy choice hai jo README mein explicitly likhi hai: grace ka matlab "galti se aaye, turant nikle toh free", discount nahi. Aur ek mutation "grace subtracted" stage 1 mein 3 tests se pakda gaya -- toh rule test se locked hai.

Ek invariant important hai: fee kabhi kam nahi hoti jab stay lamba ho. Pay-then-exit window isi par depend karti hai, aur test "never charges less for a longer stay" har 7 minute par 3 din tak teen configurations check karta hai.
why_needed: Pricing bugs seedha customer complaints aur revenue loss hain. Boundary (exactly 60 min, exactly grace) par kya hota hai, yeh interview mein zaroor poocha jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Phone call billing jaisa "per started minute": 61 second ki call 2 minute bill hoti hai. Grace waise jaise ghalat number lagne par pehle 5 second free -- par agar baat ho gayi toh poori call charge.
how_it_works: stayMs = exitAt - entryAt. Invalid ya negative -> INVALID_TIME. stayMs <= graceMs -> 0. Cap nahi -> ceil(stayMs / HOUR_MS) * rate. Cap hai -> days = floor(stayMs / DAY_MS), restHours = ceil(baaki / HOUR_MS), (days * cap + min(restHours, cap)) * rate.

Lot test "charges by the clock": 2h 8min car = 3 hours = 15000. Entry time = reserve() ka time, exit time = beginExit ka time (README).

Boundaries explicitly tested
Fee monotonic hai, toh 'pehle pay karo phir niklo' safe
disadvantages: Grace ke turant baad ek cliff hai: 10 min free, 10 min 1 ms = poora 1 hour
Night / weekend rates ya per-size rates is class mein nahi
common_mistakes: Math.floor use karna (mutation 'hours rounded down')
Grace ko stay se minus karna

question: What does 'check everything, then change state' mean in this design, and how is it proven?
answer_hinglish:
Matlab: har public method pehle woh saare checks karta hai jo throw kar sakte hain, aur PEHLI mutation tabhi hoti hai jab aage kuch fail nahi ho sakta. Result: agar ParkingError aaya, toh guaranteed "kuch nahi hua" -- koi half-done state nahi.

reserve() ko dekho: normalizePlate (INVALID_PLATE), isVehicleType (INVALID_VEHICLE), plate already taken (ALREADY_PARKED), LOT_FULL, strategy call aur STRATEGY_BUG check. Uske baad comment hai "All checks passed; from here on nothing can fail." Phir ticket freeze, spot.reserve, entries.set, ticketIdByPlate.set, aur aakhri mein changeFree (event bhi aakhri mein, taaki listeners finished change dekhein).

Exit side par bhi yahi: beginExit() pehle bill() nikalta hai -- yahan INVALID_TIME ya STRATEGY_BUG aa sakta hai -- aur spotOf() bookkeeping check, phir hi lock. Isliye clock peeche chali jaaye toh car parked rehti hai aur ticket baad mein kaam karta hai (test "keeps the car parked when the clock went backwards"). Stage 1 ki ek mutation "exit forgets the ticket before pricing" isi order ko todti thi aur 4 tests ne pakdi.

Proof ka tareeka: test/parking-lot.test.ts ka state(lot) helper -- JSON.stringify(snapshot of spots, activeTickets, availability). Har error case mein before = state(lot), failing call, phir expect(state(lot)).toBe(before). README: "every error compares the whole lot before and after."

Is design mein transactions ya rollback code nahi chahiye -- order hi guarantee hai. Ek extra fayda: JavaScript single-threaded hai, toh ek synchronous method ke beech koi aur code nahi chal sakta, aur check aur change split nahi hote.
why_needed: Agar error ke baad state half-changed ho (spot reserved par ticket nahi), toh lot dheere dheere corrupt hota hai -- spots leak hote hain jo kabhi free nahi hote. Callers ko rollback logic likhna padta.
real_world_analogy: Bank teller pehle check karta hai: ID sahi, balance kaafi, form bhara hua. Sab theek hone ke baad hi paise counter par rakhta hai. Beech mein pata chale ki form adhoora hai toh paise nikaale hi nahi gaye.
how_it_works: Har method do phases: validate (sirf reads, throw allowed) aur commit (sirf writes jo fail nahi ho sakte). Writes ka order bhi socha hua: listeners ko event sabse last. Spot transitions khud guarded hain (SPOT_STATE), par lot pehle hi itna check karta hai ki woh guard trip na ho.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: class comment "checks everything that can fail BEFORE it changes any state", reserve() ka "All checks passed" comment, beginExit() ka "may throw INVALID_TIME: nothing changed yet". test/parking-lot.test.ts: state() helper, tests "is full for trucks while compact spots are still free, and that changes nothing", "refuses the same plate twice, in any spelling, and that changes nothing", "rejects an unknown vehicle type and an invalid plate, changing nothing". PLAN.md decision "Check everything, then change state".
advantages: Error = nothing happened; caller ko rollback nahi likhna
Rollback code ki zaroorat nahi
Whole-lot comparison test har error path ko cover karta hai
disadvantages: Har naye method mein discipline chahiye; ek galat order poori guarantee tod deta hai
Kuch checks do baar hote hain (lot bhi, spot bhi)
common_mistakes: Pehle spot reserve karna, phir plate check karna
Event pehle emit karna, state baad mein
Test mein sirf error code check karna, state nahi
follow_up_questions: What would you do if a step in the middle genuinely could fail (e.g. a DB write)?
How does this relate to database transactions?
Why is the event emitted last?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Order-based atomicity sasta aur simple hai, par sirf tab kaam karta hai jab commit phase ke steps sach mein fail nahi ho sakte (in-memory Map / field writes). Jaise hi commit mein I/O aaye, yeh guarantee chali jaati hai aur transaction ya compensation chahiye.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Agar koi future developer commit phase mein kuch aisa daale jo throw kar sakta hai (jaise listener ko synchronously call karke uska error propagate karna), toh half state ban sakti hai. Isliye EventQueue listener errors pakad kar report karta hai aur change ko undo nahi karta.
advanced.alternatives: Alternative 1: try / catch ke saath manual rollback -- error-prone. Alternative 2: copy-on-write (naya state object banao, end mein swap) -- clean par har call par copy. Alternative 3: database transaction -- persistence aaye toh yahi sahi jagah hai.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: In-memory lot ke liye scale se farak nahi padta: checks O(sizes x log spots) hain. Multi-process / database mein yeh guarantee DB transaction ya conditional UPDATE mein move hogi -- README isse "not built" bolta hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Property-based test jo random operations ke baad har failure par state compare kare (invariants.test.ts random steps chalata hai). Lint rule ya code review checklist ki naye methods validate-then-commit follow karein. Persistence aaye toh same method ek DB transaction ke andar.

question: Why does the lot take an injected Clock instead of calling Date.now(), and how is ManualClock used?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki time is domain ka input hai -- fee time par depend karti hai -- aur jo input hai use inject karna chahiye, taaki tests usko control kar sakein.

src/clock.ts mein Clock interface hai: now(): number (epoch milliseconds). systemClock = { now: () => Date.now() } production ke liye, aur ManualClock tests aur demo ke liye. ParkingLot options mein clock optional hai, default systemClock. Lot sirf this.clock.now() call karta hai -- reserve() mein entryAt ke liye, beginExit() mein exitAt ke liye, quote() mein.

ManualClock ke teen methods: now(), advance(ms) -- negative ya non-finite par RangeError -- aur set(time) jo koi bhi value le sakta hai, past bhi. set() isliye hai ki clock peeche jaane ka case test ho sake.

Fayde concretely: test 2 ghante 8 minute ka stay check karta hai bina 2 ghante wait kiye -- clock.advance(2 * HOUR_MS + 8 * MINUTE_MS), fee 15000. Grace boundary par exactly 10 minute advance karke fee 0. Aur "keeps the car parked when the clock went backwards": clock.set(T0 - 1), exit -> INVALID_TIME, state unchanged, phir clock.set(T0 + HOUR_MS) aur wahi ticket 5000 deta hai.

Demo bhi ManualClock(Date.UTC(2026, 10, 22, 9, 0)) use karta hai, toh har run ka output same aata hai.

Production note: real servers par clock NTP se peeche ja sakti hai. Yahan woh case crash ya negative fee nahi deta -- INVALID_TIME aata hai aur car parked rehti hai. Monotonic clock ya server-side time source jaisa kuch is project mein nahi hai.
why_needed: Hidden Date.now() wala code test karna mushkil hai: ya toh real wait karo, ya global fake timers lagao. Injected clock se time ek normal parameter ban jaata hai.
real_world_analogy: Exam hall mein invigilator ki ghadi. Practice mock test mein teacher apni ghadi aage-peeche karke dekh sakta hai ki "time up" par kya hota hai, asli 3 ghante wait kiye bina.
how_it_works: Dependency injection: lot ko ek object milta hai jiske paas now() hai. Production mein woh Date.now() wrap karta hai, tests mein ek variable lautata hai jise test khud badalta hai. Pricing khud clock nahi dekhti -- usse entryAt aur exitAt numbers milte hain, toh pricing pure function rehti hai.
in_this_project: src/clock.ts: Clock, systemClock, ManualClock (advance, set). src/parking-lot.ts constructor: this.clock = options.clock ?? systemClock. test/parking-lot.test.ts makeLot: new ManualClock(T0). src/demo.ts: ManualClock se scripted day. PLAN.md: "Time comes from an injected Clock. Tests move time without waiting, and can make it go backwards."

Clock-backwards jaise rare case test ho sakte hain
Pricing pure rehti hai (time numbers ke roop mein aata hai)
disadvantages: Ek aur constructor option
Agar koi andar Date.now() direct call kar de toh injection bypass ho jaata hai
common_mistakes: Pricing class ke andar Date.now() call karna
Global fake timers par depend karna jo doosre tests ko affect karein

question: Why are tickets frozen, and what exactly does Object.freeze protect here?
answer_hinglish:
Ticket woh cheez hai jo caller ke haath mein jaati hai. Agar woh mutable ho, toh caller ticket.spotId = "L0-2" karke apni gaadi kaagaz par doosre spot par "shift" kar sakta hai, aur lot ki duniya aur ticket ki duniya alag ho jaayengi. Isliye reserve() ticket ko Object.freeze({...}) se banata hai.

Do layers hain. TypeScript readonly fields (Ticket interface mein sab readonly) compile time par assignment rokte hain -- par yeh sirf type check hai, runtime par JavaScript ko pata nahi. Object.freeze runtime guarantee hai: strict mode (ES modules strict hote hain) mein frozen object ki property assign karne par TypeError. Test "tickets are frozen: a caller cannot move its car to another spot" cast karke readonly bypass karta hai aur expect karta hai toThrow(TypeError), phir findByPlate("A1")!.spotId abhi bhi "L0-1".

Object.freeze SHALLOW hai. Ticket ke saare fields primitives hain (strings, numbers), toh shallow kaafi hai. Receipt mein payments array hai -- isliye commitExit use alag se Object.freeze([...entry.payments]) karta hai, aur har Payment khud bhi recordPayment mein freeze hota hai. Copy bhi zaroori hai: lot ki internal array share nahi hoti.

Aur lot internally ticket ke saath mutable cheezein (status, lock, payments) alag Entry object mein rakhta hai. Toh ticket kabhi badalta hi nahi; lost ticket par naya ticket banta hai. README mutation "ticket not frozen" stage 1 aur stage 3 dono mein 1 test se pakda gaya -- sirf ek test, toh woh test important hai.
why_needed: Public API se bahar jaane waale objects ka aliasing bug classic hai: caller ka edit library ki state badal deta hai. Freeze se yeh possible hi nahi.
real_world_analogy: Laminated ID card -- aap padh sakte ho, par usme pen se kuch likh nahi sakte. Naam badalna hai toh naya card banta hai.
how_it_works: Object.freeze(obj) properties ko non-writable aur non-configurable bana deta hai, aur naye properties add nahi ho sakte. Strict mode mein write par TypeError, sloppy mode mein chupchaap ignore. Nested objects freeze nahi hote -- unhe alag freeze karna padta hai.

Exit test r.ticket toBe(t) -- receipt mein wahi ticket object.
advantages: Runtime guarantee, sirf compile time nahi
Ticket safely share ho sakta hai (receipt mein wahi object)
Aliasing bugs impossible
disadvantages: Shallow hai -- nested data alag se freeze karna padta hai
Sloppy mode code mein write chupchaap ignore hota hai, error nahi
common_mistakes: Sirf TypeScript readonly par bharosa karna
Receipt freeze karna par payments array nahi
Internal array seedha return kar dena (copy ke bina)

question: Why are ticket ids random UUIDs instead of a simple counter?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki ticket id hi woh cheez hai jo car ko bahar nikalne deti hai. exit(ticketId), beginExit(ticketId), quote(ticketId) -- sab sirf id lete hain. Agar id guessable ho, toh koi bhi doosri car ka ticket "guess" karke us ka bill dekh sakta hai ya uske naam par exit start kar sakta hai.

reserve() mein id: randomUUID() hai (node:crypto se), comment ke saath "unguessable: a ticket id is what lets a car out". crypto.randomUUID version 4 UUID deta hai jisme 122 random bits hain, cryptographically secure source se. Test "returns a ticket with ..." check karta hai id /^[0-9a-f-]{36}$/ match kare, aur "gives every ticket a different id".

Counter ke do problem. Ek: predictable -- mera ticket 41 hai toh 40 aur 42 kisi aur ke hain. Do: PLAN.md ek aur subtle bug batata hai -- counter agar ACTIVE count par based ho (jaise "id = entries.size + 1"), toh ids repeat hote hain: ek car nikli, count kam hua, agli car ko wahi id mil gaya jo abhi kisi active ticket ka hai. PLAN.md isse mutation M18 kehta hai. README mein "counter ticket ids" break stage 1 mein 11 tests, aur stage 2 aur stage 3 re-run mein 16 tests se pakda gaya.

Same idea aur jagah bhi: lost ticket ka replacement bhi naya randomUUID leta hai, cash payment id "cash-" + randomUUID, aur har payment lock ka paymentKey bhi randomUUID. Note: yeh id secret ki tarah act karta hai, par is project mein koi authentication ya signed ticket nahi hai -- jiske paas id hai woh use kar sakta hai.
why_needed: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) ka classic case: agar resource ka id guessable hai aur id hi access deta hai, toh enumeration attack possible hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel room ki chaabi ka number agar room number hi ho (101, 102...) toh koi bhi agla darwaza try kar le. Random card key code se aisa nahi hota.
how_it_works: randomUUID -> 128-bit value, 122 random bits, format 8-4-4-4-12 hex. Collision probability practically zero, aur pichle id se agla nikalna impossible. Counter: id_n+1 = id_n + 1, toh ek id se saare ids mil jaate hain.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts: import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto"; reserve() mein id: randomUUID(); reportLost() mein replacement id; lockEntry() mein paymentKey; exit() mein `cash-${randomUUID()}`. test/parking-lot.test.ts: id format aur uniqueness tests. PLAN.md: "Unguessable ticket ids (crypto.randomUUID) ... (mutation M18)".
advantages: Enumeration / guessing practically impossible
Restarts ya multiple lots mein bhi unique
Koi shared counter state nahi
disadvantages: Lamba id -- printed ticket par QR / barcode chahiye, insaan type nahi karega
Order ka koi signal nahi (kaunsa ticket pehle bana) -- entryAt se hi pata chalta hai
common_mistakes: Active count se id banana (repeat hota hai)
Math.random() se id banana (cryptographically secure nahi)
Id ko hi authentication maan lena bina rate limit ke
follow_up_questions: Is a random id enough security for a real exit gate?
When would you prefer a sortable id like ULID?
What does an attacker gain by guessing a ticket id here?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Random id ka trade-off: security aur uniqueness milti hai, readability aur ordering jaati hai. Ek LLD mein jahan ticket id hi bearer token hai, security jeet-ti hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Counter based ids: enumeration se kisi aur ki gaadi ka bill / exit; active-count counter se duplicate ids aur do cars ek ticket par. Random id ke saath bhi agar ticket photo kheench li jaaye toh copy ban sakti hai -- isliye exit side par TICKET_BUSY lock aur lost ticket par purane id ko TICKET_REPLACED se maarna hai.
advanced.alternatives: Alternatives: HMAC-signed ticket (id + signature, server secret ke saath), short code + plate verification, ULID / UUIDv7 agar database index ke liye time ordering chahiye (random bits ke saath).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: 10x-100x par randomUUID ka cost negligible hai. Database aaye toh random UUID primary key B-tree index mein scattered inserts karta hai; tab UUIDv7 ya ULID consider karte hain -- is project mein DB nahi hai, toh yeh concern abhi nahi.
advanced.production_improvements: Printed ticket par QR, exit par rate limiting / alerting jab ek gate par bahut saare invalid ids aayein, aur plate camera se ticket ki plate match karna. In mein se kuch bhi is project mein implement nahi hai.

question: smallestFitFirst vs nearestFirst: what is the trade-off, and why is smallestFitFirst the default?
answer_hinglish:
Dono strategies sirf "kaunsa size pehle" mein alag hain; dono same index se free.nearest(size) maangti hain (nearest = lowest level, phir lowest position).

smallestFitFirst: vehicle ke fitting sizes smallest first try karo, pehla size jisme koi free spot ho uska nearest spot lo. Car pehle compact, compact khatam toh large. Fayda: large spots trucks ke liye bache rehte hain. Nuksaan: car ko door wala compact milega chahe saamne large khaali ho -- zyada walk.

nearestFirst: har fitting size ka nearest free spot lo aur unme se jo sabse paas ho (nearer() -- pehle level, phir position) woh do. Fayda: sabse chhoti walk. Nuksaan: car aakhri large spot le sakti hai, aur baad mein truck ko LOT_FULL milega jabki compact spots khaali the.

Ek hi lot par alag answer -- tested: layout [["large"], ["compact"]] mein car ko smallestFitFirst L1-1 (compact, level 1) deti hai aur nearestFirst L0-1 (large, level 0).

Default smallestFitFirst kyun: wrong choice ka cost asymmetric hai. Car ko thoda zyada chalna ek chhoti inconvenience hai; truck ka andar na aa paana lost revenue aur ek vehicle jiske liye koi doosra option nahi. Car ke paas do sizes hain, truck ke paas ek. Isliye scarce resource (large) ko protect karna better default hai. PLAN.md: "smallestFitFirst (default, keeps large spots for trucks) and nearestFirst (shortest walk)".

Ek interesting test-gap story: stage 3 mutation run mein S24 ("nearer compares only the level") pehle 0 tests se pakda gaya -- "same level" test mein compact pehle aur large baad mein tha, toh size order se luck se sahi answer aata tha. Test fix hua (large ko nearer rakha) aur ab S24 pakda jaata hai.
why_needed: Interviewer almost hamesha poochta hai "kaunsa spot doge aur kyun". Ek rule chunna aur uska cost bolna -- yahi LLD trade-off thinking hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant mein 2 log aaye: 2-seater table door corner mein hai, 6-seater gate ke paas. Host 2-seater deta hai (smallest fit) taaki 6 logon ki family aaye toh table mile -- chahe couple ko thoda chalna pade.
how_it_works: smallestFitFirst: for size in fittingSizes(vehicle): spot = free.nearest(size); if spot return. nearestFirst: best = undefined; har fitting size ka nearest lo, nearer(spot, best) ho toh best = spot. Dono O(sizes x log n) index ki wajah se.

README "Which spot" table.
advantages: smallestFitFirst: scarce large spots protected
nearestFirst: shortest walk, simple to explain
Dono plug-in, lot owner choose kar sakta hai
disadvantages: smallestFitFirst: cars door park hoti hain
nearestFirst: trucks ke liye LOT_FULL jaldi
Koi bhi strategy occupancy-aware nahi (jaise 'last 2 large spots sirf trucks')
common_mistakes: Default bina reason ke choose karna
nearer() mein sirf level compare karna (S24)
Test fixture aisa banana jo order ke luck se pass ho jaaye
follow_up_questions: How would you reserve the last N large spots for trucks?
What would 'nearest' mean with several entrances?
How did the S24 test gap hide, and how was it found?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ek greedy per-arrival decision hai: future arrivals ka koi knowledge nahi. smallestFitFirst future ke liye hedge karta hai (scarce resource bachao), nearestFirst present user ko optimise karta hai. Lot ka mix (kitne trucks aate hain) decide karta hai kaunsa better hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: nearestFirst ke saath truck-heavy lot mein cars large spots kha lengi aur trucks bahar -- LOT_FULL aayega jabki availability board compact free dikhata hai, customer confuse. smallestFitFirst ke saath motorcycle-heavy lot mein bikes compact tak jaayengi sirf jab small khatam.
advanced.alternatives: Threshold strategy (large free < N toh cars ko large mat do) -- iske liye FreeSpots ko counts dene padenge, abhi sirf nearest(size) hai. Time-of-day based strategy. Per-vehicle composite strategy (bikes nearest, cars smallest). Entrance-aware distance -- README: "one entrance", not built.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Strategy choice ka cost index ki wajah se O(sizes x log spots) rehta hai, toh 10x spots par bhi theek. Bade lots mein "nearest" ka matlab level / position se zyada (multiple entrances, lifts) ho jaata hai -- distance model badalna padega.
advanced.production_improvements: Strategy choice ko metrics se decide karna: kitni baar trucks ko LOT_FULL mila jabki chhote spots free the. Config se strategy select karna. Distances ke liye real coordinates. Yeh sab not implemented.

question: Why was the State pattern NOT used for a parking spot?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki spot ki states ka apna koi behaviour nahi hai -- sirf "kaunsa transition allowed hai". State pattern tab useful hai jab har state mein object alag tarah behave kare (har method ka alag implementation). Yahan aisa nahi hai.

PLAN.md ka stage 1 decision: spot ki do states aur do transitions the, guarded occupy / release methods wahi kaam karte hain bina har state ki class ke. Stage 2 mein teesri state reserved aayi (gate ne claim kiya, car abhi barrier ke andar nahi), tab bhi decision wahi raha: "Still guarded methods, not the State pattern (no state has behaviour of its own)."

Ab ParkingSpot mein ek private field current: "free" | "reserved" | "occupied" aur holder hai, aur chaar methods: reserve (sirf free se), confirm (sirf reserved se, aur sahi ticket), transfer (sirf occupied, sahi holder -- lost ticket ke liye), release (free nahi hona chahiye, aur sahi holder). Galat transition -> SPOT_STATE.

State pattern lagate toh: SpotState interface, FreeState, ReservedState, OccupiedState classes, har ek mein reserve / confirm / transfer / release, jisme zyaadatar "throw" hota. 4 methods x 3 states = 12 method bodies, jinme se kaafi sirf error. Yeh ceremony hai, clarity nahi. Saare transitions ek 60-line file mein ek nazar mein dikh jaate hain aur test/spot.test.ts ke 6 tests har allowed aur refused transition cover karte hain.

Kab badlunga: agar kisi state ka sach mein alag behaviour aaye -- jaise "maintenance" state jisme pricing alag ho ya events alag hon -- tab State pattern justify hoga.

real_world_analogy: Railway signal ke teen color hain, par har color ke liye alag signal post nahi banate. Ek post, ek bulb, aur ek niyam ki kaunsa color kis ke baad aa sakta hai.
how_it_works: Guarded transitions: har method pehle (current state, holder) check karta hai, phir field update. Yeh effectively ek chhoti state machine hai jo if-checks se express hui hai, class hierarchy se nahi.

question: Why did you NOT use a Singleton for the lot, a Factory for vehicles, or a Level class?
answer_hinglish:
Teeno jagah reason ek hi hai: pattern tab lagao jab woh koi problem solve kare; yahan teeno problem create karte.

Singleton: "ek building mein ek lot" sunne mein natural lagta hai, par Singleton ka matlab global mutable state. PLAN.md: "it would make tests share one global lot and block 'two lots in one process'." Is project ke tests har test mein makeLot() se naya lot banate hain apne layout, strategy aur ManualClock ke saath; Singleton ke saath ek test ka parked car doosre test mein dikhta, aur order-dependent failures aate. Aur ek company ke do lots ek process mein chalana impossible. Lot ek normal object hai jo caller banata aur pass karta hai -- dependency injection, global nahi.

Factory for vehicles: Factory tab kaam ka hai jab construction complex ho ya type ke hisaab se alag behaviour wala object banana ho. Yahan vehicle = plate + type string. PLAN.md: "there is no behaviour per type to construct." Koi Car / Truck class nahi, toh factory kya banaayegi? Type-specific cheezein data mein hain: SMALLEST_FIT table aur HourlyPricing ke rates.

Level class: "it would only wrap an array; a spot knows its level." Spot ke paas level aur position hai, availability rows (level, size) key par hain, nearest = lowest level phir position. Level class bas spots ki list rakhti -- extra indirection, koi behaviour nahi.

Interview mein main yeh bolta hoon: in teeno ka add karna aasaan hai jab zaroorat aaye (jaise per-level gates ya per-level pricing aaye toh Level class), par pehle se lagane se design heavier hota aur Singleton toh testability seedha tod deta.
why_needed: Pattern-heavy LLD answers common hain aur interviewers unhe challenge karte hain. Har pattern ka "kya problem solve karta hai" bolna, aur yahan woh problem exist nahi karti, yahi judgement dikhata hai.
real_world_analogy: Ghar mein ek hi fridge hai, iska matlab yeh nahi ki fridge ko deewar mein cement kar do (Singleton). Kal doosra fridge aaye ya repair ke liye nikaalna ho toh mushkil. Bas ek fridge rakho jo hata sakte ho.
how_it_works: Without Singleton: new ParkingLot({ layout, pricing, allocation, clock }) -- har caller apna instance, sab dependencies explicit. Without Factory: reserve(plate, vehicle) mein vehicle ek validated string (isVehicleType). Without Level: ParkingSpot(id, level, position, size) aur rows map key `${level}:${size}`.
in_this_project: PLAN.md "Patterns NOT used, on purpose" section. src/parking-lot.ts: ParkingLot constructor options, rowKey, spots array "nearest first: level, then position". src/spot.ts: ParkingSpot ke paas readonly level aur position. test/parking-lot.test.ts makeLot: har test naya lot + ManualClock. README "Design choices" PLAN.md ko refer karta hai.
advantages: Tests isolated, koi global state nahi
Ek process mein multiple lots possible
Kam classes; har class ka kaam real
disadvantages: Interviewer jo 'textbook' Level / Vehicle hierarchy expect karta hai use explain karna padta hai
Per-level features aaye toh Level class baad mein introduce karni padegi
common_mistakes: Singleton ko 'sirf ek lot hai' ke naam par justify karna
Vehicle -> Car / Truck / Bike subclasses jinme koi method nahi
Pattern ka naam lena bina yeh bataye ki kaunsi problem solve karta hai
follow_up_questions: What would make you introduce a Level class?
How would the app ensure only one lot instance per building without a Singleton?
When is a Factory actually useful in this domain?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Kam abstraction = kam indirection aur aasaan tests, par future change ke liye refactor ka cost. Yeh cost chhota hai kyunki Level ya Vehicle class baad mein local change hai, jabki Singleton hataana baad mein mehenga hota hai (har jagah global access phail jaata hai).
advanced.failure_scenarios: Singleton ke saath: test pollution (ek test ki parked car doosre mein), parallel test runs flaky, aur do lots chalaane ka business requirement aaya toh global access ke saare call sites badalne padte. Factory / Level ke saath: dead abstractions jo reader ko confuse karti hain.
advanced.alternatives: Singleton ki jagah composition root: app startup par ek lot banao aur gates / pay stations ko pass karo (gates.ts mein EntryGate constructor lot leta hai). Vehicle behaviour aaye toh discriminated union ya Strategy per type. Level behaviour aaye toh Level class jo apne spots aur rules rakhe.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Multi-lot operator (100 lots) mein Singleton seedha fail hai; har lot ek object, ek LotRegistry jo id se lot de. Level class tab useful jab levels ke apne gates, apne prices ya closures hon -- yeh project mein nahi.

question: Why are VehicleType and SpotSize string unions instead of TypeScript enums?
answer_hinglish:
src/types.ts ki pehli line hi reason deti hai: "String unions (not TS enums) so the values are plain strings in JSON, logs and tests."

Pattern yeh hai: const VEHICLE_TYPES = ["motorcycle", "car", "truck"] as const, aur type VehicleType = (typeof VEHICLE_TYPES)[number]. Isse do cheezein ek source se milti hain -- compile time ka type ("motorcycle" | "car" | "truck") aur runtime ki array jisse validate aur iterate kar sakte hain. Same SPOT_SIZES ke saath.

Fayde concretely:
- Values plain strings hain: ticket JSON mein "car" dikhta hai, logs mein "car", tests mein lot.park("A1", "car") seedha likhte hain. Numeric enum mein JSON mein 1 dikhta aur debugging mein mapping yaad rakhni padti.
- Runtime array ka use hai: isVehicleType() aur isSpotSize() includes() se untrusted input validate karte hain (INVALID_VEHICLE, INVALID_LAYOUT); HourlyPricing constructor VEHICLE_TYPES par loop karke har rate check karta hai; fittingSizes() SPOT_SIZES filter karta hai; aur SPOT_SIZES ka ORDER hi fits rule hai.
- TS enums JavaScript output mein extra object generate karte hain aur kuch build tools (isolated transpilers) ke saath quirks hain; unions sirf type hain, runtime par kuch nahi.
- Record<VehicleType, ...> se compiler har type ki entry maangta hai -- naya vehicle jodo toh SMALLEST_FIT aur rates mein missing entry compile error.

Nuksaan: enum jaisa namespace (VehicleType.Car) nahi milta, aur rename karna ho toh string literals har jagah dhoondhne padte hain -- par compiler typo pakad leta hai.
why_needed: TypeScript mein enums vs unions ek common interview sawaal hai, aur domain values ka format logs / JSON / APIs mein dikhta hai.
real_world_analogy: Form mein dropdown jisme options seedha "Car", "Truck" likhe hain, code numbers (1, 2) nahi. Jo bhi report padhe use mapping table nahi chahiye.
how_it_works: `as const` array ko readonly tuple banata hai literal types ke saath; `(typeof ARR)[number]` un literals ka union deta hai. Runtime array aur compile-time type kabhi out of sync nahi hote kyunki ek hi declaration se aate hain.
in_this_project: src/types.ts: VEHICLE_TYPES, VehicleType, SPOT_SIZES, SpotSize, isVehicleType, isSpotSize. src/pricing.ts: for (const vehicle of VEHICLE_TYPES) rate check. src/parking-lot.ts: isVehicleType (INVALID_VEHICLE), isSpotSize (INVALID_LAYOUT). test/parking-lot.test.ts: lot.park("A1", "bus" as never) -> INVALID_VEHICLE; layout mein "huge" -> INVALID_LAYOUT.
advantages: JSON / logs / tests mein readable values
Ek declaration se type aur runtime list dono
Runtime par koi enum object nahi
disadvantages: VehicleType.Car jaisa namespace nahi
Rename ke liye har literal badalna padta hai (compiler help karta hai)
common_mistakes: Type aur runtime array alag alag likhna (sync se bahar ho jaate hain)
Untrusted input ko sirf TypeScript type se 'validate' maan lena
Numeric enum jiski value JSON mein meaningless number ho
follow_up_questions: How do you validate a string from JSON is a VehicleType at runtime?
What does 'as const' do here?
When would you still choose an enum?

question: An interviewer asks you to add EV charging spots. Does that fit the ordered-size model? How would you design it?
answer_hinglish:
Seedha jawab: EV charging ek SIZE nahi hai, isliye ise SPOT_SIZES array mein daalna galat hoga. Aur yeh is project mein implement nahi hai -- PLAN.md "Not in scope" mein "EV charging spots" explicitly likha hai.

Kyun fit nahi hota: fits() ka rule linear order hai -- "bada spot har woh cheez le sakta hai jo chhota leta hai". Agar SPOT_SIZES = ["small", "compact", "ev", "large"] kar do toh rule kahega truck EV spot nahi le sakta (sahi) par motorcycle aur har car EV spot le sakti hai (shayad galat -- business chahta hai EV spot sirf EV ko mile), aur EV car ko charging spot ki zaroorat hai par order mein yeh express hi nahi hota. Size aur charging do alag dimensions hain: ek physical (kya gaadi samayegi), ek feature (charger chahiye / mana hai).

Mera design: ParkingSpot par ek alag attribute, jaise charger: boolean, aur vehicle side par "needs charging" ka flag (ya ek vehicle type). Fit rule do conditions ka AND ban jaata hai: size fit (existing fits()) AND feature rule (EV spot sirf charging-wale vehicle ko, ya policy ho toh dusron ko bhi jab bahut khaali ho). Yeh feature rule ya toh lot ka fixed rule ho, ya allocation Strategy mein jaaye.

Index par asar: FreeSpotIndex abhi ek heap per SpotSize rakhta hai aur FreeSpots sirf nearest(size) deta hai. EV ke liye key (size, charger) karni padegi, aur availability rows (level, size) se (level, size, charger). Pricing: charging ka alag rate -- PricingStrategy.fee(vehicle, entryAt, exitAt) ko spot ki info nahi milti, toh interface badalna padega ya decorator chahiye.

Yeh answer interview mein dikhata hai ki ordered-size model ki limit pata hai aur kab nayi dimension chahiye.
why_needed: Extension follow-ups hi LLD round ka asli test hain. Galat abstraction mein naya concept thoosna (EV ko size banana) baad mein ajeeb bugs deta hai.
real_world_analogy: Hotel rooms: single, double, suite ek ordered size hai. "Wheelchair accessible" ek alag feature hai -- use size list mein "double-accessible" ki tarah thoosoge toh har combination ka naya naam banana padega.
how_it_works: Current: fits(vehicle, size) = rank(size) >= rank(SMALLEST_FIT[vehicle]). Proposed: canUse(vehicle, spot) = fits(vehicle, spot.size) && featureRule(vehicle, spot). Index key size se (size, feature) tak; strategy fitting (size, feature) combinations order mein try kare.
in_this_project: Abhi kuch EV-related code nahi hai. Relevant pieces jo badalne padenge: src/types.ts (fits, SMALLEST_FIT), src/spot.ts (ParkingSpot constructor -- id, level, position, size), src/free-index.ts (heaps Map<SpotSize, MinHeap>, FreeSpots.nearest(size)), src/allocation.ts (fittingSizes), src/pricing.ts (PricingStrategy.fee signature), src/parking-lot.ts (LotLayout = SpotSize[][], rows). PLAN.md "Not in scope".
advantages: Size aur feature alag dimensions, dono apne rule ke saath
Existing fits() untouched, uske upar ek aur condition
Policy ('chargers sirf EV ke liye') strategy mein ja sakti hai
disadvantages: Index, rows aur FreeSpots interface sab badalte hain -- yeh chhota change nahi
PricingStrategy signature ko spot info chahiye -- existing strategies touch hongi
common_mistakes: EV ko SPOT_SIZES mein ek size bana dena
Har combination ka naya size naam (compact-ev, large-ev)
EV spot ko hamesha reserve rakhna chahe lot full ho (business se poocho)
follow_up_questions: Should a non-EV car be allowed in an EV spot when the lot is nearly full?
How would charging time be billed separately from parking time?
Which tests would you write first for this change?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Ordered sizes ek dimension ke liye perfect hain (ek comparison). Doosri dimension aate hi ya toh multi-attribute matching chahiye ya combinations explode karte hain. Main attribute + rule chunta hoon kyunki combinations ka count features ke saath multiply hota hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: EV ko size banaya toh: motorcycle EV spot le legi, EV car ko normal compact mil jaayega jabki charger free tha, aur availability board 'ev' ko ek size ki tarah dikhayega. Feature-based design mein risk: index key change mein stale heap entries ya galat row counts -- isliye invariants.test.ts jaisa board == availability() check har step par chahiye.
advanced.alternatives: Alternative 1: EV ko ek alag VehicleType + alag spot pool (alag lot section). Alag ParkingLot instance hi bana do EV section ke liye -- Singleton na hone ki wajah se possible hai. Alternative 2: tags / capability set per spot aur requirement set per vehicle (generic matching). Alternative 3: EV ko size mein daalna -- simplest, par galat semantics.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Features badhenge (EV, disabled-access, covered, valet) toh har combination ka heap rakhna 2^features ho jaata hai. Tab capability-based matching ya ek database query (WHERE size >= x AND charger = true ORDER BY level, position) better hai.
advanced.production_improvements: Charger ki health (broken charger wala spot EV ko mat do), charging session billing, aur spot attributes config se load karna. Is project mein inme se kuch built nahi hai.

question: Walk through ParkingLot.reserve() line by line. Why are the checks in this order?
answer_hinglish:
reserve(rawPlate, vehicle) entry ka pehla half hai (park() = reserve + confirm). Order:

1. normalizePlate(rawPlate) -- INVALID_PLATE. Sabse pehle, kyunki aage ka duplicate check normalised plate par hi sahi hai.
2. isVehicleType(vehicle) -- INVALID_VEHICLE. Runtime check, kyunki caller JS ya JSON se aa sakta hai jahan TS type nahi hota.
3. ticketIdByPlate.has(plate) -- ALREADY_PARKED. Andar ya kisi aur gate par enter ho rahi car dono cover.
4. LOT_FULL pre-check: fittingSizes(vehicle).some(size => index.nearest(size) !== undefined). Strategy se pehle, taaki "full" aur "strategy ka bug" alag rahein.
5. allocation.choose(vehicle, this.index) aur result validation -- STRATEGY_BUG agar undefined, doosre lot ka spot, free nahi, ya fit nahi.

Comment: "All checks passed; from here on nothing can fail." Phir commit:
6. Ticket = Object.freeze({ id: randomUUID(), plate, vehicle, spotId, level, entryAt: clock.now() }).
7. spot.reserve(ticket.id) -- spot reserved, holder set.
8. entries.set(ticket.id, { ticket, status: "reserved", payments: [], penaltyMinor: 0 }).
9. ticketIdByPlate.set(plate, ticket.id).
10. changeFree(spot, -1) -- availability row update aur event; comment "last: listeners see the finished change".

Order ke reasons: cheap input validation pehle, phir state-based checks, phir plug-in call, aur saari mutations ek block mein end par. Event last isliye ki listener lot ko call kare toh consistent state dekhe -- README mutation S16 "reserve emits before the spot is taken" stage 2 aur stage 3 dono runs mein 11-12 tests se pakda gaya.

Ek nuance: entryAt = reserve() ka time hai, confirm ka nahi -- printed ticket wahi dikhata hai.
why_needed: Code-level round mein interviewer ek method chun kar "line by line samjhao" kehta hai. Order ke peeche ke reasons bolna zaroori hai, sirf kya karta hai nahi.
real_world_analogy: Hospital admission: pehle ID check, phir "already admitted to nahi?", phir bed available hai ya nahi, phir ward-boy se bed suggest karwao aur check karo. Sab theek hone par hi file banti hai, bed par naam lagta hai, aur aakhri mein board update hota hai.
how_it_works: Validate phase: 5 checks, sab sirf reads (index.nearest bhi lazy deletion mein stale heap entries pop kar sakta hai, par woh observable state nahi badalta). Commit phase: 5 writes jo throw nahi kar sakte (spot.reserve tabhi throw karta jab spot free na ho, jo pehle check ho chuka).
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts::reserve, confirm, park, changeFree. src/allocation.ts::fittingSizes. Gate isse aise use karta hai: src/gates.ts EntryGate.enter -> lot.reserve() -> device -> lot.confirm() ya lot.cancel(). Tests: test/parking-lot.test.ts ke "park" describe block, test/two-phase.test.ts reserve / confirm / cancel ke liye.

Event consistent state ke baad
Checks sasta se mehenga order mein
disadvantages: Method lamba hai; validation aur commit ek hi function mein
LOT_FULL check aur strategy dono index ko query karte hain (thoda duplicate kaam)
common_mistakes: Duplicate check raw plate par karna
Ticket pehle bana kar baad mein spot check karna
changeFree pehle call karna

question: Walk through the HourlyPricing constructor and how the lot double-checks a pricing strategy. Why validate in both places?
answer_hinglish:
Do layers hain aur dono alag cheez protect karti hain.

Layer 1, HourlyPricing constructor (config time):
- for (const vehicle of VEHICLE_TYPES): har rate Number.isSafeInteger aur >= 0, warna INVALID_RATE. Loop VEHICLE_TYPES par hai, caller ke object par nahi -- toh missing rate (undefined) bhi pakda jaata hai (test "rejects a missing rate").
- graceMinutes default 0, safe integer >= 0.
- dailyCapHours agar diya toh integer 1-24 (0, 25, 2.5 tested).
- this.rates = { ...ratesPerHourMinor } -- COPY. Caller baad mein apna object badle toh pricing nahi badlegi (test "copies the rates, so changing the caller's object later changes nothing"; stage 1 mutation "rates not copied" 1 test se pakda gaya).
- graceMs = grace * MINUTE_MS ek baar precompute.

Fail fast: galat config lot start hote hi phat jaaye, pehli car ke exit par nahi.

Layer 2, ParkingLot.checkedFee (har call par): lot kisi bhi PricingStrategy ko accept karta hai, sirf HourlyPricing ko nahi. Toh lot result check karta hai -- safe integer aur >= 0, warna STRATEGY_BUG. Test ek fake strategy deta hai jo 12.5, -1, NaN lautati hai: exit aur quote dono STRATEGY_BUG, aur state same (car parked).

Dono kyun: constructor validation sirf HourlyPricing ki guarantee hai. Lot ka invariant ("paisa hamesha non-negative integer") lot ka hai, aur woh kisi plug-in par depend nahi kar sakta. Same principle allocation ke saath bhi -- STRATEGY_BUG check. Interface trust boundary hai.

Aur fee() khud INVALID_TIME phenkta hai agar exit < entry ya NaN -- yeh bhi bill() ke andar, kisi state change se pehle.
why_needed: Plug-in architecture mein host ko plug-in ke output par blind trust nahi karna chahiye, warna ek galat strategy (ya future developer ki) paise ki invariant tod degi.
real_world_analogy: Supplier khud quality check karke maal bhejta hai (constructor validation), phir bhi godown receiving par dobara check hota hai (checkedFee), kyunki godown kai suppliers se maal leta hai.
how_it_works: Constructor: validate -> copy -> precompute. Runtime: lot.bill() -> checkedFee(ticket, priceAt) -> pricing.fee(...) -> isSafeInteger && >= 0 check -> + penaltyMinor. Koi bhi throw bill() mein hota hai, jo beginExit / beginPayment / quote mein lock se pehle chalta hai.
in_this_project: src/pricing.ts::HourlyPricing constructor. src/parking-lot.ts::checkedFee aur bill. test/pricing.test.ts "HourlyPricing validation" describe (negative, fractional, NaN, missing rate, negative grace, copies rates, zero rate accepted) aur dailyCapHours rejection. test/parking-lot.test.ts "rejects a pricing strategy that returns %s, keeping the car parked". README mutation: stage 1 "fee unchecked" 3 tests, stage 3 re-run 4 tests.

Lot ka money invariant kisi bhi plug-in ke saath safe
Defensive copy se aliasing bug nahi
disadvantages: Thoda duplicate validation
Har fee call par extra check (negligible cost)
common_mistakes: Caller ke object ke keys par loop karna (missing type miss ho jaata hai)
Rates by reference store karna
Sirf apni strategy validate karna aur interface ko trust karna
follow_up_questions: Why loop over VEHICLE_TYPES instead of Object.keys(rates)?
What would happen if checkedFee were removed and a strategy returned 12.5?
Is Number.isSafeInteger enough, or should there be an upper bound?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Defense in depth vs duplication: do jagah check thoda redundant lagta hai par dono ki ownership alag hai -- constructor apne config ka owner, lot apne invariant ka owner. Removing either ek class of bugs wapas laata hai.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina copy: admin panel ka shared rates object badla aur chalti cars ka bill beech mein badal gaya. Bina checkedFee: fractional fee se paidMinor kabhi feeMinor ke barabar nahi, PAYMENT_REQUIRED loop aur car andar phasi. NaN fee: Math.max(0, NaN - paid) = NaN, due ka matlab hi khatam.
advanced.alternatives: Schema validation library (zod jaisi) se config validate karna -- project mein runtime dependencies zero rakhi gayi hain, isliye haath se. Ya branded type Money jo sirf validated constructor se bane.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Scale se validation cost nahi badalta. Badalta hai config ka source: 100 lots ke rates DB / config service se aayenge -- tab yahi constructor validation load time par galat config reject karega aur lot start nahi hoga, jo chahiye.
advanced.production_improvements: Rate changes ka audit log, rate change ka effective time (abhi naya rate sirf naya HourlyPricing object hai), aur upper bound / sanity checks (jaise rate > X par alert). Inme se kuch built nahi.

question: Explain fittingSizes and nearer() in the allocation code. How did a test gap let the S24 mutation survive?
answer_hinglish:
fittingSizes(vehicle) = SPOT_SIZES.filter(size => fits(vehicle, size)). Kyunki SPOT_SIZES smallest-first ordered hai, result bhi smallest first aata hai: car -> ["compact", "large"]. smallestFitFirst isi order par depend karti hai -- pehla size jisme free spot mile. README mutation S23 ("fitting sizes largest first") stage 2 mein 16 aur stage 3 mein 7 tests se pakda gaya.

nearer(a, b) = a.level !== b.level ? a.level < b.level : a.position < b.position. Pehle level compare, level same ho toh position. nearestFirst har fitting size ka nearest spot leta hai aur nearer() se best chunta hai.

S24 story: mutation tha "nearer compares only the level" -- matlab same level par hamesha false. Stage 3 run mein yeh 0 tests se pakda gaya, matlab survive kar gaya. Kyun? Purana "same level" test compact spot ko large se PEHLE (chhoti position par) rakhta tha. nearestFirst sizes ko compact phir large order mein dekhti hai; compact pehle best ban jaata hai, aur broken nearer() large ke liye false lautata hai -- toh compact hi rehta hai. Expected answer bhi compact tha. Sahi answer, galat reason se: size order ne luck se bacha liya.

Fix: test ne large spot ko NEARER rakha (level 0 position 2 vs compact position 5). Ab sahi nearer() large chunta hai, broken wala compact -- test fail, S24 caught (1). Test ka comment: "The large spot comes AFTER compact in size order, so only a real position comparison picks it."

Lesson: green test ka matlab yeh nahi ki woh sahi cheez test kar raha hai. Fixture ko aisa banao ki sahi answer kisi accidental order se na nikle -- aur mutation testing yahi gaps dhoondhti hai.
why_needed: Comparators chhote hote hain par unke bugs subtle hain (tie-break bhoolna). Aur mutation testing ka value samjhana senior signal hai -- coverage 100% ho kar bhi test kamzor ho sakta hai.
real_world_analogy: Exam mein answer sahi aaya par steps galat the -- teacher sirf final answer check kare toh pakda nahi jaata. Aisa sawaal do jahan galat steps galat answer dein, tab samajh aata hai student ko aata hai ya nahi.
how_it_works: Mutation testing: code mein jaan-boojh kar ek chhota bug daalo (> ko >= etc.), poora suite chalao, revert. Agar koi test fail nahi hua (survivor), toh ya test gap hai ya code ka woh hissa matter nahi karta. Yahan runner scripts repo ke bahar rakhe gaye the (README).
in_this_project: src/allocation.ts::fittingSizes, nearer, nearestFirst. test/allocation.test.ts: "compares the position when the level is the same (a nearer large beats a further compact)" -- yahi S24 fix wala test. README "The 2 that survived, and the fix" (S24 aur S26). Stage 3 mein 63 checks, 61 pehli baar caught, 2 survivors test gaps the jo close ho gaye.

Comparator ko sirf ek test cover karta hai (README: S24 exactly one test se caught at stage 2 list)

Test fixture jo accidental order se pass ho

question: Why do ParkingSpot.release() and transfer() require the holding ticket id instead of just changing state?
answer_hinglish:
Kyunki spot ko sirf woh ticket free kar sake jiske paas woh hai. src/spot.ts comment: "Needs the holding ticket, so a bug elsewhere cannot free someone else's spot."

ParkingSpot do private fields rakhta hai: current (free / reserved / occupied) aur holder (ticket id ya null). Har transition holder check karta hai:
- reserve(ticketId): sirf free spot; holder = ticketId.
- confirm(ticketId): sirf reserved AUR holder === ticketId.
- transfer(from, to): sirf occupied AUR holder === from; holder = to (lost ticket ka replacement).
- release(ticketId): free nahi hona chahiye AUR holder === ticketId; phir free, holder null.

Agar release() sirf "state = free" karta, toh lot ke kisi bug se (galat ticket ka spotId, stale entry) A ki gaadi ke chalte B ka spot free ho jaata -- aur agli car usi spot par bhej di jaati jahan B ki gaadi khadi hai. Holder check is bug ko corruption ke bajaye ek loud SPOT_STATE error bana deta hai.

Yeh defense in depth hai: lot ke paas apna check bhi hai -- spotOf(entry) verify karta hai ki spot.heldBy === entry.ticket.id, comment "Unreachable unless the lot's own bookkeeping is broken". SPOT_STATE ParkingErrorCode mein "a bug if it ever reaches a caller" ke roop mein documented hai.

Mutation evidence README se: stage 1 "release ignores the ticket" 2 tests; stage 2 S25 "spot.confirm does not check the holder" 2 tests; stage 3 survivor S26 "spot.transfer does not check the holder" -- 0 failures, kyunki koi caller transfer ko galat ticket ke saath call hi nahi karta tha. Naya spot test add hua ("transfer moves an occupied spot to a new ticket, only from its holder") aur ab S26 caught (1).
why_needed: Shared resource ko release karna sirf owner ka haq hona chahiye -- yeh wahi principle hai jo locks (sirf owner unlock kare) aur leases mein hota hai.
real_world_analogy: Locker room: locker kholne ke liye wahi chaabi chahiye jo aapko di gayi thi. Attendant bhi galti se "locker 12 khaali karo" bole toh bina chaabi nahi khulega -- galti pakdi jaati hai, kisi ka saamaan nahi jaata.
how_it_works: Guarded transition = precondition (state + owner) -> mutation. Fail par SPOT_STATE aur koi field change nahi. Test "refuses release when free or with the wrong ticket, and stays held" check karta hai ki refusal ke baad bhi state occupied aur holder t1 hai.
in_this_project: src/spot.ts::ParkingSpot (reserve, confirm, transfer, release, heldBy). src/parking-lot.ts::spotOf (heldBy check), forget() mein spot.release(entry.ticket.id), reportLost() mein spot.transfer(old.id, ticket.id). test/spot.test.ts: 6 tests, har refused transition ke baad holder same.

Ownership spot par hi enforce
Refusal ke baad state guaranteed same
disadvantages: Har call site ko ticket id pass karna padta hai
Lot aur spot dono check karte hain -- duplicate
common_mistakes: release() ko bina owner check ke likhna
Sirf state check karna, holder nahi
Kisi check ko sirf isliye untested chhodna kyunki 'koi galat call karta hi nahi' (S26)

advanced.failure_scenarios: Bina holder check: stale ticket se release -> spot free dikhta hai jabki gaadi khadi hai -> next car ko wahi spot -> do gaadiyan ek spot par, board galat. Bina transfer check: koi bhi ticket kisi aur ka spot apne naam kar sakta.
advanced.alternatives: Alternative: spot sirf boolean occupied rakhe aur ownership lot ke map mein ho (single source). Simpler, par ek hi layer -- lot mein bug toh corruption. Ya State pattern classes -- same checks, zyada code.
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Distributed / DB version mein yahi check conditional UPDATE ban jaata hai: UPDATE spots SET state = 'free', holder = NULL WHERE id = ? AND holder = ? -- affected rows 0 toh error. README isi idea ko claims ke liye mention karta hai (not built).
