question: Exercise: write a composite allocation strategy that uses a different strategy per vehicle type (motorcycles nearest, cars and trucks smallest fit), with tests.
answer_hinglish:
Requirement realistic hai: bikes ko door bhejne ka koi fayda nahi (unhe kisi bhi size mein jagah mil jaati hai aur walk chhoti honi chahiye), par cars ko smallest fit chahiye taaki large spots trucks ke liye bachein. Yeh ek naya AllocationStrategy hai -- ParkingLot mein ek line bhi nahi badalti, kyunki lot sirf interface jaanta hai.

Design: byVehicle(name, table) ek function jo Record<VehicleType, AllocationStrategy> leta hai aur ek naya strategy object lautata hai jiska choose() bas table[vehicle].choose(vehicle, free) ko delegate karta hai. Yeh Composite / delegation hai.

Record<VehicleType, ...> type ka fayda: compiler har vehicle type ki entry maangta hai. Kal "bus" type aaye toh har byVehicle call compile error dega jab tak bus ka strategy na diya jaaye -- bhoolna mushkil.

Table ko copy kar lo ({ ...table }), wahi reason jo HourlyPricing rates copy karta hai: caller baad mein apna object badle toh strategy na badle.

Safety: agar delegate koi galat spot lautaye, lot ka existing STRATEGY_BUG check pakad lega -- composite ko apna validation nahi chahiye. Aur LOT_FULL lot khud check karta hai, toh delegate ko sirf tab call kiya jaata hai jab koi fitting spot free ho.

Tests do level par: (1) test/allocation.test.ts ke style mein hand-made FreeSpots (free() aur at() helpers) se unit test -- motorcycle ko nearer compact milta hai small ke bajaye, car ko door compact milta hai paas waale large ke bajaye; (2) test/parking-lot.test.ts ke makeLot se ek test ki lot ke through bhi kaam karta hai. Note: yeh strategy repo mein abhi nahi hai -- yeh exercise ka solution hai.
why_needed: Interview follow-up "ab yeh rule vehicle-wise alag chahiye" bahut common hai. Strategy pattern ka asli fayda tab dikhta hai jab naya rule bina lot ko chhue aa jaaye.
real_world_analogy: Reception par ek coordinator jo khud decide nahi karta, bas gaadi dekh kar sahi valet ko bhejta hai: bike waala valet ek, car waala doosra.
how_it_works: byVehicle -> { name, choose(vehicle, free) { return copy[vehicle].choose(vehicle, free) } }. Lot: LOT_FULL pre-check -> composite.choose -> delegate.choose -> lot validation (free, fits, same lot) -> commit.

Composite strategy khud repo mein implement nahi hai.

Per-vehicle se zyada complex rules (time, occupancy) yahan express nahi hote

question: Exercise: add a new vehicle type 'bus' that needs a new spot size 'xlarge'. What do you change, and which tests tell you what else to update?
answer_hinglish:
Ordered-size model ki wajah se core change chhota hai, aur yahi PLAN.md ka claim hai ("Adding a size in between is one array entry"). Note: bus aur xlarge repo mein nahi hain -- yeh exercise hai.

Change 1, src/types.ts: VEHICLE_TYPES mein "bus", SPOT_SIZES ke END mein "xlarge" (sabse bada, toh aakhir mein -- order hi rule hai), aur SMALLEST_FIT mein bus: "xlarge". Bas. fits(), fittingSizes(), isVehicleType, isSpotSize, layout validation, availability rows aur FreeSpotIndex ke heaps (Map, lazily banta hai) sab apne aap naye size ko handle karte hain.

Ab dekho kya toot-ta hai -- aur yeh achha hai:
- TypeScript: Record<VehicleType, number> ki wajah se har jagah jahan rates object hai (tests, demo.ts) "bus missing" compile error (npm run typecheck).
- Runtime: vitest type check nahi karta, par HourlyPricing constructor VEHICLE_TYPES par loop karta hai, toh bus ka rate missing -> INVALID_RATE. Jo bhi test HourlyPricing banata hai (7 test files) fail hoga jab tak rate na jode.
- test/types.test.ts: hand-written expected table mein bus row nahi hai aur rows mein xlarge column nahi -- test fail hoga, aur aapko deliberately decide karna padega ki truck xlarge mein fit hota hai ya nahi. Ordered model kehta hai haan (bada spot sab le sakta hai).
- test/allocation.test.ts "fittingSizes": motorcycle / car / truck ki lists mein ab "xlarge" bhi aayega.

Business sawaal jo poochna chahiye: kya cars aur trucks ko xlarge bus bay deni chahiye? smallestFitFirst ke saath woh xlarge tabhi lenge jab chhote sizes khatam hon -- yeh usually theek hai. Agar business kahe "bus bay sirf bus ke liye", toh ordered model yeh express nahi karta -- tab EV jaisa feature rule chahiye.
why_needed: "Ek naya vehicle type add karo" LLD interview ka standard follow-up hai. Dikhana ki change kitna local hai aur compiler / tests aapko baaki jagah kaise guide karte hain, design quality ka proof hai.
real_world_analogy: Shoe store mein naya size 12 aaya: shelf ke aakhir mein ek khana jodo. Jo bhi size chart (test) haath se likha hai use update karna padega -- aur woh achha hai, kyunki chart wala insaan dekhega ki size 12 kis-kis ko fit karta hai.

Test table ko formula se generate karna, taaki woh automatically 'pass' ho jaaye

question: How would you add new pricing policies (night rates, weekend rates, per-size rates) to this design, and what invariants must any new PricingStrategy keep?
answer_hinglish:
PricingStrategy interface ek method hai: fee(vehicle, entryAt, exitAt) -> non-negative integer minor units. Naya pricing = naya class / object, ParkingLot nahi badalta. Night / weekend rates bilkul is signature mein fit hote hain: entryAt aur exitAt epoch ms hain, toh strategy stay ko time slots mein tod kar har slot ka rate laga sakti hai. Yeh is project mein implement nahi hai -- sirf HourlyPricing hai.

Per-size rates (large spot mehenga) is signature mein NAHI aate: fee() ko spot ka size nahi milta, sirf vehicle. Toh ya interface badlega (ticket ya spot size pass karo -- lot ke paas Ticket hai jisme spotId hai), ya size ko vehicle se approximate karo. Interface change ka matlab hai HourlyPricing aur test fakes sab touch honge -- isliye interviewer ko pehle bolunga ki yeh breaking change hai.

Invariants jo har strategy ko maanne hain:
1. Result non-negative safe integer -- lot checkedFee se enforce karta hai (STRATEGY_BUG).
2. Pure / deterministic: same input, same output. Lot quote() aur beginExit() alag waqt par fee call karta hai; agar strategy andar Date.now() ya random use kare toh quote aur bill mel nahi khayenge.
3. Monotonic: lamba stay kabhi sasta nahi. Yeh sabse subtle hai. Lot ka pay-then-exit window logic bill = fee(now) - paid karta hai; agar fee kam ho sakti toh difference negative hota (code clamp karta hai Math.max(0, ...), par phir customer ne zyada pay kiya). HourlyPricing ke liye yeh test "never charges less for a longer stay" se proven hai. Night discount jaisa rule ("raat 10 ke baad flat 100") galti se is invariant ko tod sakta hai -- 9:50 par exit 150, 10:05 par 100. Isliye naye strategy ke liye bhi wahi monotonic test chalana chahiye.
4. Exit < entry par INVALID_TIME, negative fee nahi.
why_needed: Pricing sabse zyada badalne wali business requirement hai. Interface ki limit (kya input milta hai) aur hidden invariants (monotonic) samajhna hi senior answer hai.
real_world_analogy: Restaurant ka menu card badalna aasaan hai (naya card chhapo), par ek rule hai jo kitchen manta hai: zyada khaana kabhi kam bill nahi ho sakta, warna "happy hour" mein log order badal ke system game kar lenge.
how_it_works: Lot ka flow: bill(entry, now) -> priceAt (window ke andar last payment ka time, warna now) -> checkedFee(ticket, priceAt) + penalty -> due = max(0, fee - paid). Naya strategy sirf fee() replace karta hai; baaki sab lot ka hai.

Decorator se policies compose hoti hain
Lot ka checkedFee har strategy par safety net
disadvantages: fee() ko spot size nahi milta -- per-size pricing ke liye interface change
Monotonic invariant code mein enforce nahi, sirf test se
Timezone (UTC vs local) ka decision strategy ke andar chhupa

Bada interface (poora Ticket ya spot) = zyada power, par strategies lot ke data model se coupled. Main pehle decorator / composition try karta hoon aur interface tabhi badalta hoon jab sach mein naya input chahiye.

Impure strategy: quote() aur beginExit() alag fee dikhayein. Fractional result: STRATEGY_BUG aur car exit nahi kar paayegi jab tak strategy fix na ho.

question: This is an in-memory library. If you had to put it behind an HTTP API with a database, which design decisions carry over and what has to change?
answer_hinglish:
Pehle honest scope: is project mein database, HTTP API, UI aur real payment provider nahi hain -- PLAN.md "Not in scope" aur README "NOT implemented" dono yeh kehte hain. Sab kuch ek Node process mein, memory mein hai. Toh yeh answer design discussion hai, built cheez nahi.

Jo carry over hota hai:
- Domain model: ParkingSpot states, Ticket fields, fits() rule, ordered sizes -- yeh tables aur columns ban jaate hain.
- Strategies: AllocationStrategy aur PricingStrategy pure logic hain; HourlyPricing seedha server par chalegi. Allocation ka "nearest free spot of a size" DB query ban sakta hai (ORDER BY level, position LIMIT 1).
- Money in minor units: DB mein integer / bigint column, float nahi.
- ParkingError codes: HTTP layer ke liye perfect -- errors.ts comment khud "an HTTP layer later" mention karta hai. LOT_FULL / ALREADY_PARKED jaise codes conflict-type responses ban sakte hain, INVALID_PLATE validation error, SPOT_STATE / STRATEGY_BUG server bug.
- Unguessable ids: randomUUID ticket ids bina badlaav ke.
- Injected Clock: server time ek jagah se.

Jo badalta hai:
- "Check everything, then change state" ki guarantee abhi JavaScript ke single-threaded synchronous methods se aati hai. Multiple API servers ya processes par yeh nahi chalega. README: claim ko database mein le jaana padega -- conditional UPDATE ya spot par unique constraint -- "the same idea, moved to where the state lives". Not built.
- Validate-then-commit ek DB transaction ban jaata hai, kyunki commit phase mein ab I/O hai jo fail ho sakta hai.
- Frozen objects ki jagah API responses (DTOs) -- immutability ka matlab ab "ticket row ko client edit nahi kar sakta".
- Stuck reservations: README kehta hai ki agar gate process mar jaaye toh reservation kabhi clean nahi hoti (no expiry sweep). DB version mein expiry time + sweeper chahiye.
why_needed: LLD round ka aakhri sawaal aksar "isko production mein kaise le jaoge" hota hai. Yahan clear bolna ki kya built hai aur kya nahi, aur kaunsi guarantee kis mechanism par tiki hai -- yahi senior answer hai.
real_world_analogy: Ek chhoti dukaan jahan ek hi cashier hai -- do log ek saath aakhri packet nahi le sakte kyunki cashier ek time par ek hi customer dekhta hai. Branch kholi aur cashiers 5 ho gaye, toh stock register central chahiye jisme "packet mera" ek entry se lock ho.
how_it_works: Abhi: HTTP nahi, ek process, lot ke methods synchronous -> check aur change ke beech koi aur code nahi. Future: request -> API handler -> DB transaction { select / conditional update spot WHERE state = 'free'; insert ticket } -> commit -> response; ParkingError code -> HTTP status mapping.
in_this_project: src/parking-lot.ts class comment (synchronous methods, check before change). src/errors.ts comment "an HTTP layer later". README "Concurrency" ("This is safe inside ONE Node process ... Not built") aur "NOT implemented (after stage 3)" list. PLAN.md decision "TypeScript, a library with no runtime dependencies, in memory. An LLD round is about classes and responsibilities, not storage or HTTP." aur "Not in scope".

-- illustrative, NOT in the repo: the in-memory "check then change" claim moved into the database
UPDATE spots
   SET state = 'reserved', holder = :ticket_id
 WHERE id = :spot_id AND state = 'free';
-- 0 rows updated -> someone else took it: pick again or LOT_FULL

-- one plate, one ticket (the ALREADY_PARKED rule) as a constraint
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX one_ticket_per_plate ON tickets (plate) WHERE status <> 'closed';

Error codes HTTP mapping ke liye ready
Clear boundary: library pure, I/O bahar
disadvantages: Concurrency guarantee in-process hai; DB ke saath dobara design karni padegi
Reservation expiry / crash recovery abhi nahi hai
common_mistakes: Sochna ki in-memory 'single-threaded so safe' guarantee multiple servers par bhi chalegi
Paisa float column mein store karna
Error message strings ko API contract bana dena, codes ke bajaye
follow_up_questions: Which ParkingError codes map to 409, 400, 404 and 500?
How would you clean up reservations whose gate crashed?
Would you keep strategies in the API server or in the database?

advanced.architecture_tradeoffs: Library ko I/O-free rakhna (pure domain + injected clock / strategies) testing ke liye best hai, par concurrency ki guarantee runtime (single thread) se aati hai. Production mein yeh guarantee DB ko deni padti hai -- domain logic ko 'functional core' ki tarah rakho aur DB transaction ko 'imperative shell'.
advanced.failure_scenarios: Do API servers same last spot ke liye in-memory check karein -> dono reserve, do tickets ek spot par. Server crash between reserve aur confirm -> spot hamesha reserved (README: no expiry sweep). DB write fail commit phase mein -> half state, jab tak transaction na ho.
advanced.alternatives: Single-writer design: ek lot ke saare writes ek process / actor / queue se (lot ka in-memory model as-is chalta rahe, bas ek owner). Ya DB-first design jahan saare rules SQL constraints mein. Ya event sourcing jahan har change ek event (EventQueue ka idea extend).
advanced.scale_10x_100x: Ek lot ke writes per second chhote hote hain (gates ki speed), toh single-writer per lot 100 lots tak bhi easy scale karta hai -- har lot ka alag partition. Read side (availability boards) cache / pub-sub se fan out.
advanced.production_improvements: Persistence + transactions, reservation expiry sweeper, idempotent API (payments ke liye already idempotency key design hai), error code -> HTTP status mapping, auth for gate devices, aur observability. In mein se kuch bhi is project mein built nahi hai.
